text.name: Hi there, My name is Yutong Wu 雨潼 (Yǔtóng, /yü-toong/).
text.intro: I'm a neuroengineer in practice and a natural scientist at heart. My background is in computational cognitive science and biology at Wellesley College, with research and coursework at MIT and the Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics.
text.qtitle: Two long-term questions I'm interested in are:
text.q1: How do biological systems perceive and understand the physical world, and how can engineered systems or technology be inspired by such discoveries?
text.q2: How should technology be designed and applied to augment a person's cognition and abilities over the long term, in a shape the nervous system is already used to?

bioBlocks.label: Name
bioBlocks.html: Hi there, my name is Yutong Wu 雨潼 (Yǔtóng, /yü-toong/)

bioBlocks.label: Introduction
bioBlocks.html: A neuroengineer in practice and a natural scientist at heart. I explore how living systems perceive the world and how technology can expand the ways we sense, understand, and act. My work moves between Multimodal Biosensing, Neural Decoding, and Embodied Interaction.

bioBlocks.label: Background
bioBlocks.html: I have a background in Computational Cognitive Science (magna cum laude, ’26) and Biology from Wellesley College, with research and course experience at MIT and the Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics.

bioBlocks.label: Current work
bioBlocks.html:
I'm currently a development engineer at a BCI startup building toward an sEEG-based brain foundation model. My work focuses on:

  • building a non-invasive interface ecosystem with sEMG, EEG, eye tracking, force feedback, and physiological health signals for applications in assistive technology and human-robot interaction
  • researching a brain foundation model that learns transferable neural representations to decode human intent and enable adaptive physical interaction.

bioBlocks.label: Long-term questions
bioBlocks.html:
Two long-term questions I'm interested in are:

  1. How do biological systems perceive and understand the physical world, and how can engineered systems or technology be inspired by such discoveries?
  2. How should technology be designed and applied to augment a person’s cognition and abilities over the long term, in a shape the nervous system is already used to?

bioBlocks.label: Training
bioBlocks.html: I'm grateful to my training in biology for showing me the wondrous world of how organisms and their societies actually work; in computer science for teaching me how to formalize and build; and in philosophy for giving me an abstract and reflective foundation for the nature of my inquiry and creation <3

bioBlocks.label: Outside the lab
bioBlocks.html: Outside the lab, I enjoy photography, learning languages, playing music (Guzheng), and theater. I've also been co-running an arts education NGO for children since 2021.
